source_text:
Intimate Wear Market Innovations: Smart Fabrics, Inclusive Design, and Sustainable Comfort
Introduction

The intimate wear industry is experiencing a meaningful transformation as consumers increasingly prioritize comfort, functionality, personal expression, and responsible manufacturing. Traditionally shaped by established silhouettes, seasonal fashion trends, and conventional sizing systems, the category is expanding toward products that address diverse body types, changing lifestyles, and individual preferences. Advances in textile engineering, digital design, and manufacturing processes are creating new opportunities for brands to rethink how intimate apparel is developed, produced, and experienced.

From breathable everyday essentials to adaptive undergarments and intelligently engineered fabrics, innovation is becoming an important factor in product differentiation. Consumers are no longer evaluating intimate wear solely on appearance. Fit consistency, skin comfort, durability, material transparency, and versatility increasingly influence purchasing decisions. These evolving expectations are encouraging manufacturers to reconsider both product design and the broader value chain.

1. Advanced Fabrics Are Redefining Everyday Comfort

Performance Materials and Intelligent Textile Engineering

Fabric innovation is one of the most influential developments in intimate apparel. Modern consumers expect underwear, bras, shapewear, and sleepwear to provide support without restricting movement or compromising comfort. To meet these expectations, manufacturers are exploring lightweight knits, stretch-recovery fibers, moisture-managing textiles, and seamless construction techniques.

Microfiber blends, modal, responsibly sourced cotton, and selected regenerated cellulose fibers offer different combinations of softness, breathability, and flexibility. Material selection depends on the intended application, since a supportive sports bra requires different structural properties from lightweight sleepwear or everyday underwear.

Innovations in knitting technology also enable manufacturers to create targeted compression, improved elasticity, and smoother edges within a single garment. These techniques can reduce bulky seams and minimize friction in areas where conventional construction may cause discomfort.

Temperature Regulation and Moisture Management

Consumers increasingly seek intimate apparel that performs comfortably throughout changing temperatures and activity levels. Moisture-wicking finishes, breathable fabric structures, and strategically positioned ventilation zones can help manage perspiration and improve the wearing experience.

However, performance claims must be supported by appropriate testing. Breathability, moisture transfer, colorfastness, and repeated-wash durability should be evaluated under relevant conditions. This is particularly important for garments marketed for sensitive skin or extended daily wear.

2. Seamless Construction and 3D Design Improve Product Development

Seamless manufacturing is gaining attention because it can produce garments with fewer traditional seams, smoother profiles, and reduced material waste in certain applications. Circular knitting machines and advanced bonding methods allow designers to develop underwear and bras with carefully controlled stretch, shaping, and support.

Three-dimensional design tools are also changing the product development process. Digital garment simulations can help teams assess fit, fabric behavior, and construction details before creating physical samples. When combined with accurate body measurements and physical testing, these tools may shorten development cycles and reduce unnecessary sampling.

For manufacturers, the principal advantage is greater flexibility. Product teams can test multiple design variations, evaluate construction alternatives, and identify potential fit issues earlier in the process.

Nevertheless, digital simulations cannot fully replace physical fitting across diverse bodies and movement patterns. Successful implementation requires reliable material data, representative fit models, and feedback from actual wear trials.

3. Inclusive Sizing and Adaptive Intimate Apparel Expand Consumer Choice

Designing Beyond Traditional Size Categories

Inclusive design is becoming a central consideration in intimate apparel development. Conventional sizing systems can overlook differences in breast shape, torso length, hip proportions, asymmetry, and individual support preferences. As a result, consumers may experience inconsistent fit even when purchasing products labeled with the same size.

Brands are responding by expanding size ranges, refining cup and band combinations, and developing different support levels for specific body proportions. Adjustable straps, flexible closures, wider bands, and carefully engineered stretch zones can help accommodate a broader range of needs.

Better fit systems also benefit retailers by potentially reducing avoidable returns and improving consumer confidence. Achieving these outcomes requires more than adding larger sizes to an existing pattern. Garment grading, support structures, material tension, and construction details must be reassessed throughout the size range.

Adaptive Features and Functional Design

Adaptive intimate wear represents another important area of product development. Front closures, magnetic fastenings, simplified adjustment systems, and soft, low-profile construction can make garments easier to put on and remove for people with limited mobility or dexterity.

Post-surgical garments and specialized maternity or nursing bras also illustrate how functional requirements can influence design. In these categories, accessibility, adjustability, and appropriate support may be more important than conventional fashion details.

The opportunity lies in treating accessibility as a design principle rather than a niche afterthought. Consumer consultation and practical wear testing are essential to ensure that products address real needs instead of relying on assumptions.

4. Sustainability Is Reshaping Materials and Manufacturing

Environmental considerations are influencing decisions about fiber selection, production efficiency, packaging, and garment longevity. Intimate apparel presents specific sustainability challenges because products often combine several fibers, elastics, closures, and bonded components. These combinations can make recycling more complicated.

Responsible Material Selection

Organic cotton, recycled fibers, and selected lower-impact cellulose materials offer potential benefits when their production methods and supply chains are carefully evaluated. However, no material is automatically sustainable in every application. Water use, energy consumption, chemical processing, durability, and end-of-life options all affect its overall environmental profile.

Manufacturers can improve material decisions by documenting fiber composition, establishing supplier requirements, and assessing environmental performance across relevant production stages.

Durability and Waste Reduction

Longer-lasting garments can reduce the frequency of replacement, making durability an important aspect of responsible design. Reinforced stress points, resilient elastics, colorfast dyes, and construction that withstands repeated washing can help extend product life.

Digital pattern planning, improved cutting efficiency, and demand forecasting can also reduce manufacturing waste and excess inventory. Smaller production runs and more responsive replenishment systems may help brands avoid overproduction, although their effectiveness depends on production costs, lead times, and demand variability.

Clear care instructions and transparent product information further support informed purchasing decisions.

5. Personalization and Digital Retail Are Changing Shopping Experiences

Digital retail tools are creating new ways for consumers to discover, evaluate, and purchase intimate apparel. Fit questionnaires, guided measurement tools, product comparison features, and virtual assistance can help shoppers navigate categories that often involve sizing uncertainty.

Artificial intelligence can support product recommendations by identifying relationships between stated preferences, fit feedback, and product characteristics. When implemented responsibly, these tools may help consumers narrow their options and reduce the frustration associated with repeated trial and error.

However, intimate apparel requires particular attention to privacy. Body measurements and fit preferences can be sensitive information. Businesses should explain what data they collect, obtain appropriate consent, limit unnecessary retention, and provide meaningful controls over personal information.

Personalization should also remain practical. Consumers may value a recommendation based on support level, fabric feel, coverage, and intended use more than a complex technology feature that adds little to the purchasing experience.

6. Intimate Wear Market Innovations: Key Opportunities for Brands

[Intimate wear market innovations](https://www.pristinemarketinsights.com/intimate-wear-market-report) are creating opportunities for businesses that combine material performance, inclusive product engineering, and thoughtful consumer engagement. The strongest developments are likely to emerge where technology solves a clearly defined customer problem rather than serving as an isolated novelty.

For established manufacturers, upgrading knitting equipment, improving quality-control systems, and integrating digital product development may strengthen operational efficiency. Emerging brands can differentiate themselves through specialized fit categories, transparent material sourcing, or products designed for underserved consumer groups.

Retailers also have an important role to play. Detailed sizing guidance, consistent product descriptions, realistic imagery, and accessible customer support can help bridge the gap between online product presentation and actual wearing experience.

Meanwhile, manufacturers and retailers must balance innovation with affordability. Advanced materials, specialized construction, and broader size inventories can increase development and production costs. Careful assortment planning, supplier collaboration, and measurable product testing are therefore essential to commercial success.

7. Challenges That Will Shape Future Development

Despite promising opportunities, innovation in intimate apparel faces several practical challenges. New materials may require specialized equipment, while complex designs can introduce additional quality-control requirements. Inconsistent sizing standards across brands also make it difficult for consumers to transfer their fit knowledge from one product to another.

Sustainability claims present another challenge. Businesses need credible evidence to distinguish measurable environmental improvements from superficial messaging. Similarly, performance claims concerning odor control, moisture management, or skin comfort should be supported by appropriate testing and clearly defined conditions.

Supply chain resilience will remain important as companies manage fluctuating material costs, changing consumer demand, and varying supplier capabilities. Businesses that invest in product testing, supplier transparency, and continuous feedback are better positioned to identify problems before they become widespread.

Conclusion

The intimate wear industry is moving toward a more considered approach to product development, where comfort, technical performance, inclusivity, and environmental responsibility increasingly intersect. Advances in fabric engineering, seamless construction, adaptive design, and digital retail are creating practical opportunities to improve both consumer experiences and manufacturing processes.

Future progress will depend less on adopting technology for its own sake and more on translating innovation into dependable products. Brands that prioritize fit accuracy, material quality, privacy, durability, and authentic consumer needs can build stronger relationships with their audiences. As expectations continue to evolve, thoughtful design and measurable performance will remain essential to long-term competitiveness in the intimate apparel sector.

create-pr skill suggests package names as PR title scopes, which check-pr-title rejects
## Summary

Agent-authored PRs fail `check-pr-title` about two times as often as other PRs. This PR aligns the `n8n:create-pr` skill and the title conventions with the validator that CI runs (`n8n-io/validate-n8n-pull-request-title` at `8aad045`, v2.5.0).

**Data.** PRs opened from 1 April to 30 September 2026, from public GitHub data:

- 1,129 PRs have the "Generated with Claude Code" footer. Each one is matched with one "n8n team" PR without an AI marker, from the same month and size bucket.
- `check-pr-title` failed on the first red commit of 52 agent PRs and 27 matched PRs.
- In the 52 agent failures, the causes in the first title are:
  - a scope that the validator does not accept (29);
  - a lowercase first letter in the summary (27);
  - a past-tense first verb (4);
  - a ticket or PR number (3).

  One title can have more than one cause.
- The rejected scopes are package names: `instance-ai` (7), `cli` (3), `evals` (3), `docker` (2), `playwright` (2), and others.

**Causes in the skill.**

- Step 4 asks "Scope: Which package/area is affected?". Agents answer with a package name.
- The scope list does not include `ai-builder`. The validator accepts it, and 247 merged PRs in this period use it.
- The validation regex accepts any scope without a hyphen. The validator rejects unknown scopes. The old regex accepts 9 of the 36 agent titles that CI rejected.
- The same regex is cached in `.agents/skills/community-pr-readiness-check/reference/checks.md`.

**Changes.**

- `.agents/skills/create-pr/SKILL.md`:
  - Add `ai-builder`.
  - Say that only the listed scopes pass, and that a package name is not a scope.
  - Change step 4: pick a scope from the list, or omit it.
  - Replace the scope part of the regex with the validator's scope list.
  - Add the rules that were missing: past tense, ticket and PR numbers, and the position of `(no-changelog)`.
- `.github/pull_request_title_conventions.md`:
  - Add `ai-builder` to the scope list and to the diagram.
  - Correct the `* Node` note. The validator matches the node display name (`getAllNodesDisplayNames`), and the examples already show display names.
- `.agents/skills/community-pr-readiness-check/reference/checks.md`:
  - Use the same scope list in both cached regexes.
  - Describe the scope list in the recap below the regexes. The recap still said that scopes exclude hyphens.

**Not changed: `revert`.** The conventions and the readiness check describe `revert:` titles. The pinned validator (`src/constants.js` at `8aad045`) does not have `revert` in `TYPES`, so a `revert:` title can fail `check-pr-title`. This PR keeps `revert` as it is. The team can decide which source is correct.

## How to test

- Compare the scope list with `SCOPES` in `src/constants.js` of `n8n-io/validate-n8n-pull-request-title` at `8aad045`. This is the version pinned in `.github/workflows/ci-check-pr-title.yml`.
- The new regex was compared with the validator rules on 10,012 PR titles. These are the titles of the PRs above, plus the first titles of renamed PRs.
  - The new regex agrees on 98.1% of the titles; the old regex agrees on 94.1%.
  - Most of the remaining differences are titles with a leading space, or titles with text after `(no-changelog)`.
- The new regex rejects 33 of the 36 agent titles that CI rejected. The titles come from rename events.

## Related Linear tickets, Github issues, and Community forum posts

Closes #40885

## Review / Merge checklist

- [ ] I have seen this code, I have run this code, and I take responsibility for this code.
- [x] PR title and summary are descriptive. ([conventions](../blob/master/.github/pull_request_title_conventions.md))
- [ ] [Docs updated](https://github.com/n8n-io/n8n-docs) or follow-up ticket created.
- [ ] Tests included.
- [ ] PR Labeled with `Backport to Beta`, `Backport to Stable`, or `Backport to v1` (if the PR is an urgent fix that needs to be backported)

MVP next: strict TS compliance + real supplier and net-margin pipeline after verified national gate
## Objective
Unblock Tender AI Kazakhstan MVP while national-regime proof adapter remains under Issue #22. Implement an **offline, modular TS/supplier/margin pipeline with a strict fail-closed national gate**, so future PASS_TO_TS lots can be processed without waiting for further architectural work.

### Scope: one small PR
1. A pure decision contract: only authoritative, fresh, fully bound per-lot `PASS_TO_TS` enters TS research. `HOLD_NATIONAL`, `SKIP`, missing evidence, and manual K-column values without source verification never enter automatic supplier research. No `GO` inferred.
2. Define typed normalized result shape for: lot identity/announcement, original TS source/link/hash and criteria list, actual candidate Brand+Model+Partnumber, criterion-by-criterion evidence and `TS_COMPLIANCE_100_PERCENT` (never fabricated), three distinct supplier quotes with price/date/stock/lead time evidence, delivery/taxes/certifications/fees/contingency, total landed cost, net profit, margin, markup, break-even, and GO/REVIEW/NO-GO. Missing cost items -> REVIEW; `GO` only when margin >=20% *net*, all proofs present, acceptable competition/legal constraints and TS compliance=100%.
3. Offline tests for malformed/duplicate TS criteria, weak price sources, outdated quotes, missing costs, optimistic profit assumptions, contradictory supplier stock, national gate UNKNOWN/YES, replay/idempotency and zero Sheets/Secrets mutations.
4. Document a tiny manual-first flow: user-authorized lot only -> gate PASS_TO_TS -> full TS extraction -> supplier sourcing. Avoid broad national scan and avoid search spam. Preserve explicit repository constraints and existing 79 product categories.

### Guardrails
- Do not fake product matches, suppliers, quoted prices, 100% TS or profit. No direct external purchases/bids.
- Keep `FULL_SCAN_DISABLED`, no daily trigger, no API key change, no Apps Script publish, no autonomous writes to Google Sheets or `NATIONAL_GATE`.
- Prepare a concise PR with tests and clear paths to later production integration.
- Base on current main after PR #24 commit `27d3cfda48d8b105351ebeb3e368d4c225191e8c`. Coordinate with Issue #22 but do not conflate the permission gate with technical/financial GO.
- Deliver short actionable output in Kazakh.

AI Marketing & n8n Automation Specialist for chill life — Potential Long-Term Partnership 
 Hi, I’m Beth Levis, founder of chill life, a purpose-driven lifestyle brand. 
 We believe happier people create healthier communities. Our apparel, products, and initiatives promote positivity, mental fitness, and meaningful real-life connection. Two key areas of our work are encouraging healthier youth sports culture and helping people take daily breaks from technology to be more present. 
 I’m looking for an experienced AI marketing and automation specialist who can help translate this mission into consistent storytelling, audience growth, and measurable sales. 
 What I’m looking to build 
 A coordinated marketing system using n8n and AI tools such as Claude or OpenAI to: 
 ● Develop content grounded in our brand voice, values, and product offerings. 
 ● Create and repurpose social posts, video scripts, and email campaigns. 
 ● Manage a content calendar and approval process. 
 ● Connect relevant tools across our Shopify store, email marketing, and social channels. 
 ● Track performance and use those insights to improve campaigns. 
 Preserving the authenticity of chill life’s message is essential. The system should support thoughtful storytelling, with my review and approval built into the process. 
 Who would be a strong fit 
 Someone who combines technical skill with marketing judgment and has already built successful AI marketing workflows for an apparel, lifestyle, or consumer-product brand. 
 You should be able to show what you built, explain the strategy behind it, and share measurable results—particularly sales, conversions, customer acquisition, or repeat purchases. 
 An interest in positivity, mental fitness, youth sports, and building a brand with purpose would be a meaningful advantage. 
 Engagement and partnership 
 I’m open to discussing a project-based or ongoing engagement. For the right person, there may also be an opportunity to explore a longer-term strategic partnership, including potential equity tied to an agreed role, contribution, and results. Scope and compensation would be discussed together. 
 Please send me a private message with: 
 1. Relevant consumer-brand projects and the results achieved. 
 2. Examples of n8n and AI workflows you have built. 
 3. Your role in both marketing strategy and implementation. 
 4. How you would approach an initial project for chill life. 
 5. Your availability, pricing, and interest in a longer-term partnership. 
 Learn more about the brand:  https://chill-life.com

 Beth Levis

source_text:
Golden Client E2E — parcours boutique→retrait, preuves documentaires B2C/B2B et recette humaine
## Objectif produit
Transformer la Golden actuelle (cockpit 10 frontières, commande synthétique créée déjà payée) en **recette complète boutique → client final → finance**, comprenant **documents clients + preuves B2B et contrôles agents**. Un seul fil `market + order_reference + trace_id` lie Playwright, verdicts humains, écrans réels, documents et oracles backend. Ne pas refaire les centaines de tests existants ; les réutiliser.

## État vérifié sur main au 13/10/2026
- `public/golden-e2e-cockpit.html` offre 10 étapes et les boutons `golden-create` / `golden-advance` ; il commence sur une commande **déjà préparée**, pas sur la visite client/OTP/checkout. `services/golden-e2e-cockpit.js` projette les faits métiers, pas les documents.
- Le cockpit peut actuellement afficher `Golden certifié` sur **10 clics humains** indépendamment des preuves backend (faux vert).
- Route `/admin/golden-e2e` présente dans `bootstrap/html-routes.js` ; entrée de menu Canonical à confirmer/brancher sous autorité admin.
- `routes/admin-order-360.js` : POST `golden-create` / `golden-advance` sont **interdits en production** (garde NODE_ENV). Ne jamais contourner cette garde.
- `features/documents.feature.js` / `routes/documents.js` : accès privé client sous `/api/auth/me/documents` ; actuellement la liste client expose factures et reçus de remboursement. `transaction_documents` contient aussi des justificatifs internes. Aucune URL documentaire publique, aucun PDF envoyé via WhatsApp.
- Réconciliation Hub distincte du fulfillment ; réception réelle validée par agent Hub ; remise client distincte de disponibilité relais.
- Source : `docs/doctrine/DOCTRINE_DOCUMENTS_TRANSACTIONNELS_KOMERCE.md` et `docs/audits/KOMERCE_E2E_CERTIFICATION_GAP.md` (audit point de départ, à réévaluer sur HEAD).

## Scénario fil rouge — automatisation puis recette humaine
1. **Client navigateur réel** : market KM/CM/CG, catalogue sourcé et affichage en français, fiche produit/variante/prix/stock, panier individuel ou liste figée.
2. **Client authentification OTP** : émission réelle sur sandbox contrôlé, réception/validation, expiration, erreur, tentative concurrente. Pas de faux « OTP reçu » à partir d'une simple réponse simulée.
3. **Checkout** : choix relais, devise, prix figé, création commande depuis la vraie boutique (pas d'INSERT préalable). Variantes wallet, cash relais, PSP sandbox si disponible, Mobile Money selon market/capacité.
4. **Confirmation** : événement de paiement confirmé (pas simple `pending`), commande/reçu, **facture client** (PDF immuable privé, bon destinataire), historique / Mon Komerce / notification.
5. **Achat fournisseur** : `purchase_lines` → PO SKU/SOI exact, groupement, doublons/concurrence, fournisseur/quantités/devise. Contrôle du bon de commande B2B (trame/état réel, PDF seulement si un système en produit un).
6. **Exécution fournisseur** : preuve de commande et de paiement fournisseur, confirmation/accusé externe **si réellement accessible**, matching/rejeu.
7. **Expédition fournisseur** : numéro tracking, preuve d'expédition / BL ou facture fournisseur si transmis ; aucun document présumé présent ; suivi fournisseur ne signifie **pas** réception Hub.
8. **Réception physique Hub** : agent Hub confirme unité/quantité/état sur vraie surface autorisée ; pièce de réception / écart / réserve rattachée à la PO. C'est le Hub qui confirme physiquement.
9. **Transit → douane → relais → remise** : pièces de transport/douane (si requises), réception relais réelle, scan QR/code/autorisation, preuve de retrait client ; disponible ≠ remis.
10. **Clôture** : coûts achat/transport/douane, cash garde si applicable, réconciliation et règlement Market (si applicable), documents comptables, absence d'écart non soldé.

### Variantes intégrées au même moteur
- Client individuel / liste partagée figée / deux sessions concurrentes.
- Paiement réussi, échoué, expiré, callback dupliqué/désordonné, annulation et remboursement.
- Stock limité et 2 achats simultanés ; divergence réservation / commande payée.
- KM/CM/CG, devise/prix/catalogue/français/relai, desktop et mobile ; ne promettre un PSP ou provider L6 que si sandbox réellement accessible.
- PO groupées/partielles, manque fournisseur, réception Hub partielle, incident douane, colis endommagé, échec document, retrait non autorisé.

## Matrice documentaire obligatoire et agent responsable
| Transition | Justificatif à contrôler | Source/autorité | Si absence |
|---|---|---|---|
| Paiement confirmé | facture B2C PDF privée (après événement confirmé) | documents + orders | BLOQUANT, diagnostic Finance/Documents |
| Remboursement confirmé (variante) | avoir / reçu remboursement privé | refunds/documents | BLOQUANT |
| PO créée | PO persistée + représentation B2B si disponible | purchasing | agent Achats : vérifier génération/export ; ne pas inventer un PDF |
| Fournisseur confirmé/payé | référence fournisseur + preuve de débit + accusé/facture si disponible | purchasing/provider | agent Achats : récupérer/rapprocher ; contrôle manuel traçable |
| Fournisseur expédie | fulfillment / tracking + BL ou preuve transport **si fournie** | provider/purchasing | agent Achats ou Logistique : demander pièce, tracer absence |
| Hub reçoit | réception physique horodatée/quantités/agent + preuve de réception | Hub | agent Hub : contrôle réel, écart/réserve, BLOQUANT si absent |
| Douane/transit | déclaration / facture douane / justificatif transport selon exigibilité | logistics/customs | transitaire : rapprocher ou déclarer manquant |
| Relais reçoit | scan / statut réception physique réel | Relay | agent relais : contrôle, anomalie si non reçu |
| Client retire | scan de retrait autorisé + `pickup_proof` si émis | Relay/documents | agent relais : corriger ou signaler |
| Finance clôture | rapprochements coûts/règlement/cash, pièces nécessaires | Finance | comptable : investigation ouverte, aucun faux vert |

**Statuts documentaires** : `NON_DU`, `ATTENDU`, `DISPONIBLE_A_VERIFIER`, `VERIFIE`, `CONTROLE_MANUEL_REQUIS`, `MANQUANT_BLOQUANT` (projection de recette, pas cycle métier parallèle). Pour chaque pièce : événement déclencheur, exigibilité selon market/provider, source canonique, référence/URL authentifiée ou identifiant, horodatage, acteur, hash si disponible, verdict, raison d'absence, tâche agent / preuve d'intervention ; `non applicable` ne vaut pas `verifié`. Ne jamais fabriquer de PDF externe, de BL ou de facture fournisseur.

## Lots de livraison (PRs petites, gouvernées)
- [ ] **A — accès / cadrage** : menu admin Canonical → /admin/golden-e2e avec vérification des droits, scénario client réel distinct du parcours synthétique de frontière ; rendre visibles le market et les niveaux de preuve L0–L6.
- [ ] **B — client Playwright / humain** : réutiliser E2E boutique+OTP+checkout+partage, sessions clients et vrais écrans ; opérateur vérifie la continuité, sans injection directe de commande payée.
- [ ] **C — documents** : projection read-only par fil/order/PO : document source, éligibilité, statut, URL privée autorisée, responsable d'une preuve fournisseur absente ; distinguer B2C et B2B.
- [ ] **D — terrain** : cliquer sur les **actions réelles** avec rôle agent Hub/transitaire/relais (ou simulator non-prod explicitement étiqueté) ; pas de mutation depuis un écran de projection ni bypass de permissions.
- [ ] **E — verdict de certification** : `VERT` uniquement si preuves backend canoniques + documents obligatoires + étapes automatiques réellement exécutées + validations humaines + absence d'incident bloquant ; `NON EXECUTE`/mock/staging absent restent visibles, aucun faux vert.
- [ ] **F — scénarios négatifs et marchés** : concurrence, remboursements, webhooks, plusieurs marchés, mobile, documents conditionnels, rapport exportable et liens vers vraies interfaces.

## Garde-fous / définition de fini
- **Playwright avant humain** : l'humain joue d'abord le client (catalogue→OTP→paiement→confirmation), puis l'agent aux seules frontières physiques autorisées. La suite du client après paiement est essentiellement notification et suivi, pas clic forcé.
- Aucun reset destructif ; fixture dédiée, environnement isolé ; aucun achat/fonds réels ; aucun accès client à une pièce B2B ou fuite inter-market.
- Tests L3 mockés != L4 réel navigateur+serveur+DB != L5 staging != L6 prestataire sandbox. Afficher ces niveaux explicitement.
- Un `golden-create` ne remplace pas un vrai checkout ; les 10 étapes actuelles restent utiles comme **sous-recette**.
- S'assurer que les anomalies cash collections / statut shipping décrites par l'audit historique sont vérifiées sur main et corrigées si encore présentes.
- Avant modifications : `npm run agent:context -- --pack ui --feature dashboard`, `npm run agent:context -- --pack service --feature documents`, `npm run arch:impact -- ...`, tests ciblés, **`npm run pr:preflight` vert avant chaque PR**, CI et merge selon `AGENTS.md`.
- Terminé seulement quand une commande issue du navigateur traverse les vraies frontières jusqu'au retrait/clôture, que les documents sont consultables sous permissions correctes ou qu'un contrôle agent explicite résout leur absence, et que le verdict refuse tout faux vert.

## Amendement P0 — Sourcing et Raffinerie obligatoires avant la vraie boutique (13/10/2026)

La Golden complète ne démarre **jamais** d'un produit artificiellement injecté dans le catalogue. Chaîne requise : SOURCE FOURNISSEUR → SOURCING RÉUSSI → RAFFINERIE RÉUSSIE → REMISE AU CATALOGUE → PUBLICATION ET VENDABILITÉ MARKET → VRAIE BOUTIQUE → CLIENT → ACHAT → FOURNISSEUR → LIVRAISON → CLÔTURE.

Le sourcing et la raffinerie peuvent avoir déjà eu lieu avant l'ouverture du navigateur ; la Golden doit alors vérifier leurs faits persistés, leur identité et leur provenance. Un parcours acheté sur un produit préexistant est une certification partielle, et pas une certification complète de la source au client.

### Quatre preuves bloquantes

- SOURCE_PROVED : source réelle identifiée, capture/observation fraîche, identité exacte Offer/Unit/SOI, et passage sourcing réellement attesté, pas un seed.

- REFINERY_PROVED : passage et résultat réels, contrôles qualité et données produit/variantes/images, décisions de rejet ou d'acceptation journalisées, pas de bypass.

- CATALOG_RELEASE_PROVED : remise au catalogue par l'owner, SKU/variante exacts, publication et vendabilité Market, prix/devise/relais corrects, observés dans la boutique réelle.

- CUSTOMER_ORDER_PROVED : filiation jusqu'aux order_items et purchase_lines/PO, correspondance exacte product_sku_id et supplier_unit_ref/SOI, aucune substitution de SKU similaire.

### Cockpit et tests

Ajouter des étapes et des liens directs Sourcing → Raffinerie → Catalogue → Produit 360 → Boutique → Commande → PO fournisseur ; exposer verdict et preuve propre à chaque frontière. Rejeter une Golden complète si preuve absente, produit seed direct, raffinerie non attestée, publication simulée ou SKU/SOI divergente. Cas négatifs : source inconnue, article rejeté, stock/prix évoluant après sourcing, Market non publié, concurrence et replay. Ne pas relancer du sourcing pour chaque achat : proposer une exécution contrôlée séparée pour certifier la source au client avec vrais faits persistant sur environnement isolé. Réutiliser les propriétaires Sourcing, Raffinerie/Catalogue, Purchasing sans créer une vérité parallèle. Aucun achat, publication externe ou paiement live sans autorisation.

## Décision — Assainissement préalable des produits de test
Avant une Golden source→client, inventorier les produits actuellement créés directement par les tests ou seeds Sourcing, en distinguant environment, market_id, product_id/SKU, provenance et liens avec commandes/PO/paiements. Ne JAMAIS effectuer de DELETE global ni de RESET, ni toucher à la production. En DB éphémère dédiée de recette, retirer seulement les fixtures identifiées explicitement, via les services propriétaires et le mécanisme de nettoyage approprié ; si un produit a des liens métiers ou historique, le désactiver/écarter de la Golden plutôt que le supprimer. Vérifier les FK et le nombre avant/après, conserver les sources et traces d'audit. Dans la Golden, la liste de produits éligibles doit être vide au départ puis peuplée exclusivement par un sourcing réel + passage raffinerie + publication Catalogue attestés. Fournir d'abord inventaire et dry-run chiffré pour validation avant toute action destructive ; aucune suppression exécutée par la présente issue.

Show HN: Tracon (air traffic control for subagents)
My Claude Code workflow usually involves... a lot of subagents. I make one Opus model coordinate work as my tech lead, it dispatches subagents using models appropriate for the task into their own git worktrees, and then I try to multitask and do something else while they run. I'd been finding lately (particularly with Opus 5.5) that there was a ton of drift and instances of subagents not doing anything and it was evading the attention of the TL despite the instructions I gave it to have them report in at a regular cadence. Running tracon in a split terminal is my new personal workflow. It gives me early indicators when things start going off the rails (ex. blocked on a prompt, idle, looping on a failing command, simultaneous edits to files other subagents are editing, drifting off the brief, etc.) and I can interrogate the subagent's workflow and by pressing n the main agent gets a note to make a call on how and if to correct it. Read-only and runs on your machine: it tails transcripts in ~/.claude/projects/ and checks each worktree with ps, lsof, and git -- only thing that leaves your machine is what the Haiku judge reads for classification (or optionally you can turn that off with --no-judge). I've found it super useful for the game I'm building and figured others in the community might also find it useful. If you just want to give it a spin without committing:     uvx tracon --demo
  
macOS and Linux, Python 3.12+, MIT. (Not affiliated with Anthropic.)

source_text:
Microsoft SharePoint node (v1): `Return All` silently drops `$filter` and `$expand=fields` on `Item → Get Many`
### Bug Description

### Environment

- n8n version: 2.27.4 (self-hosted)
- Node: `n8n-nodes-base.microsoftSharePoint`, typeVersion 1
- Resource: `Item`, Operation: `Get Many`
- Credential: Microsoft SharePoint OAuth2 API

### Summary

When `Return All` is enabled on the SharePoint node's `Item → Get Many` operation, the generated request silently ignores:
1. The `Filter by Formula` field (no `$filter` is sent to the API), and
2. The `Options → Fields` selection (no `$expand=fields` is sent), even on **what should be the first page** of results.

Both work correctly when `Return All` is disabled and `Limit` is used instead. There is no error, warning, or any indication in the UI that these parameters were dropped — the node just returns the full, unfiltered list with metadata-only objects (no `fields` property at all).

### To Reproduce

1. Add a Microsoft SharePoint node, Resource = `Item`, Operation = `Get Many`.
2. Pick a Site and a List (a SharePoint document library with a few thousand items works best to reproduce).
3. In **Options → Fields**, select `Fields`.
4. In **Filter by Formula**, enter a condition on a non-indexed column, e.g.:
   ```
   fields/FileLeafRef eq 'some-exact-file-name.xlsx'
   ```
5. Enable **Return All**. Execute the node.
6. Observe: the node returns **every** item in the list (e.g. 4063 items in our case), not just the one matching the filter. No `fields` object is present on any returned item.
7. Now disable **Return All**, set **Limit** to e.g. 100, keep the same filter. Execute again.
8. Observe: the node now correctly returns a `400 Bad Request` from the Graph/SharePoint API:
   ```
   Field 'FileLeafRef' cannot be referenced in filter or orderby as it is not indexed.
   Provide the 'Prefer: HonorNonIndexedQueriesWarningMayFailRandomly' header to allow this...
   ```
   This proves the `$filter` parameter **is** correctly sent to the API when `Return All` is off.
9. Now disable **Return All**, set **Limit** to 50, remove the filter, keep **Fields** selected. Execute again.
10. Observe: the response correctly contains a `fields` object per item (e.g. `fields.FileLeafRef`, `fields.FileDirRef`, etc.), confirming `$expand=fields` **is** correctly sent when `Return All` is off.

### Expected behavior

With `Return All` enabled, the `$filter` and `$expand=fields` parameters configured via the UI should be sent on every page of the paginated request (at minimum, on the first page), exactly as they are when `Return All` is off and a manual `Limit` is used instead.

### Debug Info

### Actual Behavior

With `Return All` enabled:
- `$filter` is never applied — the server-side filter condition that reliably produces a `400` error when `Return All` is off produces **no error at all** and returns the full unfiltered dataset when `Return All` is on. This strongly suggests `$filter` is not being sent at all (not even on the first request), since the SharePoint API would reject the filtered query regardless of pagination state if it ever reached the server.
- `$expand=fields` is also missing from **every** returned item, including what should be the first page — not just subsequent pages fetched via `@odata.nextLink`.

### Evidence Table

| Return All | Limit | Filter set | Fields option | Result |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| ON | — | No | Yes | All 4063 items returned, **no `fields` key present on any item** |
| ON | — | Yes (`FileLeafRef eq '...'`) | Yes | All 4063 items returned (unfiltered), **no error** |
| OFF | 100 | Yes (`FileLeafRef eq '...'`) | Yes | **400 Bad Request** — "field not indexed" (proves filter *was* sent) |
| OFF | 50 | No | Yes | 50 items returned, **`fields` object correctly present** on each |

### Root Cause (hypothesis, not confirmed against source)

Looking at `packages/nodes-base/nodes/Microsoft/SharePoint/v1/descriptions/item/getAll.operation.ts`, the `returnAll` property's routing config defines a `pagination.request` override:

```ts
pagination: {
  type: 'generic',
  properties: {
    continue: '={{ !!$response.body?.["@odata.nextLink"] }}',
    request: {
      url: '={{ $response.body?.["@odata.nextLink"] ?? $request.url }}',
      qs: {
        $select: '={{ !!$response.body?.["@odata.nextLink"] ? undefined : $request.qs?.$select }}',
      },
    },
  },
},
```

This `request.qs` object only ever defines `$select`. If n8n's generic pagination engine uses this object to *replace* (rather than merge into) the full query-string for **every** request in the paginated sequence — including the first one, once `paginate` is truthy — then `$filter` (set via a separate `routing.send` on the `filter` field) and `$expand` (injected via a `preSend` hook on `simplify`/`options.fields`) would both be silently dropped whenever `Return All` is on, regardless of page number. This matches 100% of the observed behavior above.

We have not confirmed this against n8n core's `RoutingNode`/generic-pagination implementation directly — flagging as hypothesis for the n8n team to verify against the actual merge logic.

### Workaround Used

Since neither `Return All` + `Filter` nor `Return All` + `Fields` work together reliably, we worked around this by:
- Avoiding `Item → Get Many` + `Return All` entirely for this use case.
- Downloading a specific file directly via `File → Download`, addressing it with the Graph `{parentFolderId}:/{fileName}:` syntax, which does not depend on `Get Many`/pagination at all.

### Operating System

Linux

### n8n Version

2.27.4

### Node.js Version

24.0.0

### Database

SQLite (default)

### Execution mode

main (default)

### Hosting

self hosted

[software-development-practices:nist-ssdf] github/gh-aw-firewall repository guidance Repository-observable SSDF controls for `github/gh-aw-firewall` are generally strong at commit `360f0f904b1824dbffa1288d8dee58db94e903ab`: pinned GitHub Actions, scheduled CodeQL/dependency/supply-chain scans, SBOM/cosign coverage for container images, and regression-oriented test gates are all present. The main evidence-backed gap is release integrity for non-container CLI assets: I found checksum validation for `awf-*` binaries and `awf.tgz`, but not a repo-observable signature or provenance verification path for those assets themselves. This review is advisory and non-binding; it does not prove security, compliance, certification, endorsement, or SSDF conformance. **Action:** Maintainer should assign this issue to Copilot to add signed or attested verification for CLI release assets and update installer/docs; accept when a release publishes verifiable signatures or provenance for `awf-*` binaries and `awf.tgz`, `install.sh` or setup paths validate them, and release documentation shows the verification flow. - Critical finding: container release integrity is stronger than CLI release integrity today (`.github/workflows/release.yml`, `docs/image-verification.md`, `install.sh`, `docs/releasing.md`). - Critical finding: repository-observable detection and prevention controls are broad and active in source (`.github/workflows/codeql.yml`, `dependency-audit.yml`, `supply-chain-scan.yml`, `test-coverage.yml`, `.github/dependabot.yml`). - Critical metric: 1 promoted backlog item met the threshold for an evidence-backed repository change in this run.
Agent prompt Implement a release-integrity improvement for `github/gh-aw-firewall` focused on SSDF PS.2.1 / PS.3.1 / PS.3.2. Requirements: 1. Extend the release pipeline so `awf-linux-x64`, `awf-linux-arm64`, `awf-darwin-x64`, `awf-darwin-arm64`, `awf-bundle.js`, and `awf.tgz` ship with verifiable signatures or provenance that is generated in CI and published with the release. 2. Update `install.sh` and any setup/install path that currently trusts only `checksums.txt` so it validates the new signature/provenance material before installation, while still failing closed on mismatches. 3. Update release/install docs to show how users verify the CLI assets, parallel to the existing container-image verification guidance. 4. Add or update focused tests that cover failure paths for tampered assets/metadata. 5. Keep existing container signing/SBOM behavior intact. Deliverables: - Workflow changes in `.github/workflows/release.yml` - Installer/setup changes (`install.sh`, `action.yml`, or both as needed) - Documentation updates (`docs/releasing.md`, `README.md`, `docs/image-verification.md` or a better-named CLI verification doc) - Tests proving the verification path fails closed
Assessment metadata, scope, and limitations ### Metadata - Target repository: `github/gh-aw-firewall` - Analyzed commit: `360f0f904b1824dbffa1288d8dee58db94e903ab` - Target snapshot source: local `target/` checkout plus bounded GitHub metadata reads - Source verification date: `2026-10-13` - Final SSDF baseline used: `NIST SP 800-218 Version 1.1 (final, February 2022)` - Official URLs: - `https://csrc.nist.gov/projects/ssdf` - `https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/sp/800/218/final` - `https://doi.org/10.6028/NIST.SP.800-218` - Machine-readable marker: - `` ### Scope and assumptions - Repository-observable review only: committed files in `target/` and bounded accessible GitHub metadata. - Assessed against the current final SSDF baseline above. The NIST SSDF project page also references `SP 800-218A` as a final SSDF community profile for generative AI and dual-use foundation models, but it augments `SP 800-218` and was **not** treated as a replacement baseline for this repository review. - Findings are risk-based and scoped to evidence visible in this repository snapshot; absence of repository evidence is **not** proof that an organizational control does not exist. ### Inaccessible or non-repository evidence - Branch protection / rulesets details were not readable with the available credential (`gh api repos/github/gh-aw-firewall/branches/main/protection` returned `403 Resource not accessible by personal access token`). - GitHub security feature state, private security alerts, secret-scanning alerts, advisories, internal training records, personnel/process evidence, and private incident-response artifacts were not assessed. - Workflow files provide evidence of intended controls, but this run did not establish historical execution success for every workflow.
PO / PS / PW / RV practice-to-evidence matrix ### Practice matrix | Practice / task focus | Status | Repository-observable evidence | Evidence limits / assumptions | Concrete improvement and risk reduced | |---|---|---|---|---| | `PO.1.1`-`PO.1.3` — define and communicate software-development security requirements | `PARTIAL` | `docs/security.md` defines disclosure expectations; `docs/awf-config-spec.md`, `docs/network-isolation-design.md`, and `docs/image-verification.md` document security-relevant product and release requirements; `README.md` surfaces supported security behaviors. | No visible organization-wide policy register, annual review record, or third-party acquisition/security-contract evidence. | Consolidate repository-scoped secure-release requirements for CLI and container artifacts in one maintained policy/doc so release obligations do not drift. Reduces missed integrity requirements. | | `PO.2.1`-`PO.2.3` — roles, responsibilities, training, leadership commitment | `HUMAN_REVIEW_REQUIRED` | `.github/CODEOWNERS` assigns a maintainer; `CONTRIBUTING.md` and `docs/security.md` define contributor/security reporting paths. | Training, management commitment, and role review cadence are not repository-observable. | Maintain explicit code ownership and review paths; confirm separately whether secure-development roles and training are formalized. Reduces reliance on implicit ownership. | | `PO.3.1`-`PO.3.3` — supporting toolchains and artifacts | `OBSERVED` | `.github/workflows/codeql.yml`, `dependency-audit.yml`, `supply-chain-scan.yml`, `test-coverage.yml`, and `release.yml` codify automated checks; actions are commit-pinned; release artifacts include `checksums.txt`, `containers.txt`, and schemas. | Runtime hardening and monitoring of hosted CI infrastructure itself are not directly visible. | Preserve pinned-action and artifact-producing workflows; add equivalent provenance coverage for CLI assets. Reduces toolchain tampering blind spots. | | `PO.4.1`-`PO.4.2` — criteria for security checks and protected evidence | `PARTIAL` | High/critical dependency findings fail in `.github/workflows/dependency-audit.yml`; PR-built container CVEs fail in `supply-chain-scan.yml`; coverage regressions fail in `test-coverage.yml`; CodeQL runs on push/PR/schedule. | Criteria exist across workflows, but I did not find one central repo doc that ties gates, exceptions, and approval criteria together. | Keep machine-enforced thresholds close to the workflows and document exceptions centrally when they are allowed. Reduces inconsistent triage. | | `PO.5.1`-`PO.5.2` — secure development environments and hardened endpoints | `PARTIAL` | `docs/network-isolation-design.md`, `docs/security.md`, and product docs describe isolated execution, deny-by-default egress, and credential isolation patterns; several workflows use `persist-credentials: false` and least-privilege `permissions`. | Developer endpoint hardening, MFA, runner segmentation, and operational monitoring evidence are mostly outside the repository. | Continue isolating credentials and minimizing runner permissions; verify separately that endpoint and runner hardening matches the documented model. Reduces unreviewed change risk. | | `PS.2.1` — provide a mechanism to verify software release integrity | `GAP_FOUND` | `docs/image-verification.md` documents cosign verification for container images. `install.sh` and release docs validate CLI assets with `checksums.txt`, and `.github/workflows/release.yml` generates that checksum file, but I did not find repo-observable signatures or provenance verification for `awf-*` binaries or `awf.tgz`. | There could be external verification material not visible here, but none was referenced in repository docs, workflows, or installer paths reviewed. | Publish and validate signed or attested verification material for CLI release assets. Reduces risk that a tampered binary and matching checksum on the same release channel evade detection. | | `PS.3.1`-`PS.3.2` — archive releases and maintain/share provenance | `PARTIAL` | `.github/workflows/release.yml` publishes binaries, tarballs, schemas, `checksums.txt`, and `containers.txt`; container images are signed and SBOM-attested; some enclave/cloud-hypervisor artifacts include provenance files. | Equivalent provenance/signature coverage for all CLI assets was not found. Long-term archive controls beyond GitHub Releases are not visible. | Extend provenance/signature publication from selected artifacts to the CLI release set. Reduces incomplete release-forensics coverage. | | `PW.1.1`-`PW.1.3` — design to meet security requirements and mitigate risks | `OBSERVED` | `docs/network-isolation-design.md`, `docs/security.md`, `docs/authentication-architecture.md`, `docs/sandbox-design.md`, and `docs/enclaves-architecture.md` capture security architecture and threat-model reasoning. | This does not prove that every change receives formal threat modeling. | Preserve design docs and keep threat-model updates coupled to security-relevant changes. Reduces design drift. | | `PW.2.1` — independent review of design against security requirements/risk | `PARTIAL` | `.github/CODEOWNERS` supports review; `.github/workflows/security-review.md` exists as a dedicated threat-model/security review workflow; release/process docs contain review-oriented checks. | Could not confirm mandatory execution or independence for every design-affecting change. | Define when security design review is required and link resulting artifacts to changes. Reduces missed design regressions. | | `PW.4.1` / `PW.4.2` / `PW.4.4` — acquire, maintain, and verify reused software/components | `OBSERVED` | `.github/dependabot.yml` updates npm, Docker, and GitHub Actions dependencies; `dependency-audit.yml` and `supply-chain-scan.yml` verify dependency risk; `package-lock.json` and `docs-site/package-lock.json` lock dependencies. | Supplier assurance outside what is codified in repo tooling is not visible. | Keep automated update + audit loops in place and include new ecosystems as they are added. Reduces stale dependency exposure. | | `PW.5.1` — secure coding practices | `OBSERVED` | `package.json` includes `eslint-plugin-security`; source contains dedicated lint/test rules (for example `eslint-rules/no-unsafe-execa.js`); `codeql.yml` enables `security-extended,security-and-quality`. | Secure-coding training and review quality are not directly observable. | Preserve secure-coding automation and add targeted rules when new risk classes emerge. Reduces recurring implementation flaws. | | `PW.6.1`-`PW.6.2` — hardened compilation/interpreter/build configuration | `OBSERVED` | `release.yml` pins actions, signs container images with cosign, generates SBOMs, disables cache for security-critical agent image builds, and runs seccomp verification checks for agent images. | Build-host hardening and provenance for all non-container binaries were not fully visible. | Extend hardened-build outputs with CLI-asset provenance/signatures. Reduces build artifact substitution risk. | | `PW.7.1`-`PW.7.2` — review/analyze human-readable code | `PARTIAL` | `codeql.yml`, ESLint security rules, `.github/CODEOWNERS`, and numerous tests provide automated/static review layers. | Mandatory human review enforcement could not be confirmed via rulesets/branch protection. | Keep static analysis current and validate human-review enforcement separately. Reduces code-level vulnerability escape. | | `PW.8.1`-`PW.8.2` — test executable code and record findings | `OBSERVED` | `test-coverage.yml`, `build-test.md`, smoke/test workflows, integration/unit tests in `package.json`, and security-focused scan workflows show extensive executable and workflow-level testing. | I did not inspect historical issue-tracking linkage for every discovered failure. | Preserve fail-closed security tests and keep coverage focused on security-critical paths. source_text:
Show HN: Flopper is a hardware explorer for AI infrastructure and beyond
Hello! I built Flopper to make it easier to compare GPUs and understand the tradeoffs for workloads for AI and beyond. When researching GPUs from say Nvidia, AMD, and Huawei, I kept running into the same problem: specs were scattered across datasheets, and matching them to available configurations, vendors, and prices was cumbersome and a bit weird and frankly annoyingggg! AMD made me make an account :( So I started a place to bring that information together. Flopper lets you compare GPU specs, including TDP and compute throughput in terms of flops/tops, alongside estimates for AI workloads or other compute workloads (say, ~FP32 based) I recently added pricing data from dozens of providers to help track how prices change over time. Getting reliable quotes for systems like the NVL72 is still particularly difficult tbh, not sure how I can tell you how much that costs easily due to them being behind large procurement contracts and big multi-nationals. One thing that's become fairlyyyy clear is the interest in consumer cards and local LLMs. The bigger challenge is connecting advertised specs to real-world performance. In our testing so far, I’ve seen roughly 85% of advertised throughput, but that’s a ballpark observation for the workloads I’ve tested, not a general rule and so variable (power, cooling, workload etc). I'm considering a CLI that lets people run benchmarks and submit results, potentially using MLPerf as an automation? That way, we can all compare quoted performance with the workload, configuration etc. I'd love feedback: what information is missing, how can I improve it? And what would you need to see to trust a community-submitted benchmark? Corrections and additions also very welcome - some of the measurements are best efforts (and simple multiplications) but I hope it's of some use. Thanks for looking :)

How Does the Micron MT29F1G08ABAFAH4-AAT NAND Flash Memory Work?
NAND flash memory is an essential technology in modern electronic systems, providing non-volatile data storage that retains information even when power is disconnected. It is widely used in embedded systems, automotive electronics, industrial equipment, and digital devices that require reliable memory solutions.
The Micron [MT29F1G08ABAFAH4-AAT](https://globx.eu/products/micron/mt29f1g08abafah4-aatf) NAND Flash Memory is a 1Gb single-level cell (SLC) NAND flash memory device designed for applications that need dependable data storage and parallel memory access. With an 8-bit data bus, a 3.3V I/O interface, and an operating temperature range of -40°C to +105°C, it is suited to demanding embedded and automotive environments.
Understanding how this NAND flash memory works helps engineers select appropriate storage components for electronic system design, firmware storage, and industrial applications.

**What Is the Micron MT29F1G08ABAFAH4-AAT?**
The MT29F1G08ABAFAH4-AAT is a non-volatile [NAND flash memory](https://doodleordie.com/profile/globxoffical) component manufactured by Micron Technology. It stores digital information in memory cells that retain their programmed state without continuous electrical power.
The device provides a 1-gigabit storage capacity, organized as 128M × 8 bits. Its parallel interface allows a compatible processor or memory controller to transfer data through an eight-bit bus.
Unlike volatile memory such as SRAM and DRAM, NAND flash memory preserves stored information when the system shuts down. This makes it useful for storing firmware, configuration data, and other information required when an electronic device starts operating.

**How Does NAND Flash Memory Work?**
NAND flash memory stores information by controlling the electrical charge within specialized semiconductor memory cells. These cells represent digital data through different electrical states.

The MT29F1G08ABAFAH4-AAT uses single-level cell technology, meaning each memory cell stores one bit of information.
Its operation can be understood through three main processes.

1. Storing Data in Memory Cells
During programming, the memory device applies controlled electrical conditions to place charge into the storage structure of selected memory cells. The resulting electrical characteristics represent the programmed data.
In SLC NAND flash, each cell represents either a logical 0 or a logical 1. Because each cell stores one bit, SLC technology offers a straightforward storage arrangement compared with multi-level NAND technologies.
This design is useful in embedded applications where predictable memory behavior and endurance are important considerations.

2. Reading Stored Information
When a processor needs information, it sends the appropriate command and address to the NAND flash memory. The device accesses the selected location and determines the stored bit values by sensing the electrical characteristics of the memory cells.
The retrieved data is transferred through the eight-bit parallel interface.
A compatible controller or processor coordinates the read operation and uses the returned information for tasks such as loading firmware, accessing configuration settings, or retrieving stored program data.

3. Erasing and Reprogramming Data
NAND flash memory generally erases data in blocks rather than allowing arbitrary individual bytes to be overwritten directly.
When existing information must be replaced, the system typically erases the relevant block before programming new data into it. Pages are used for read and program operations, while blocks contain multiple pages.
The controller or firmware must manage these operations correctly, including handling bad blocks and monitoring data integrity where required.

**What Makes SLC NAND Flash Different?**
Single-level cell NAND flash stores one bit per memory cell. Other NAND technologies, including MLC, TLC, and QLC, store multiple bits per cell.
The main difference is how many electrical states each cell must distinguish.
SLC NAND uses two principal states, making the interpretation of stored data simpler than in technologies that use more states per cell. SLC memory is therefore often selected for applications that prioritize endurance, reliable operation, and consistent embedded storage behavior.
However, actual performance and endurance depend on the device specifications, operating conditions, and the system's memory management strategy.

**Applications of the Micron MT29F1G08ABAFAH4-AAT**
The combination of SLC NAND technology, parallel access, and an extended operating temperature range makes this memory component relevant to several types of electronic systems.

**Automotive Electronics**
Automotive electronic control units may need non-volatile storage for firmware, calibration information, and configuration data. A memory device rated for operation from -40°C to +105°C can be considered for suitable automotive designs, provided all electrical, qualification, and reliability requirements are satisfied.

**Industrial Embedded Systems**
Industrial controllers, monitoring equipment, and automation systems often need persistent storage for program code and system settings. NAND flash memory can provide this storage without requiring continuous power.

**Firmware and Boot Storage**
Embedded platforms can use NAND flash to store firmware images and other startup information. The processor or bootloader must support the memory interface and the device's command and timing requirements.

**Communication and Control Equipment**
Networking devices, industrial communication modules, and electronic control products may use parallel NAND memory for firmware and data storage. The suitability of this specific device depends on capacity requirements, controller compatibility, and the application's reliability targets.

**Advantages of the Micron MT29F1G08ABAFAH4-AAT**
Several characteristics make this component worth considering during embedded memory selection.

**Non-volatile storage**: Stored information remains available when the power supply is disconnected.
SLC memory architecture: One bit per cell provides a simpler storage scheme and is commonly associated with higher write endurance than higher-density multi-bit NAND technologies.

**Parallel data interface:** The eight-bit bus supports data transfer to compatible memory controllers and processors.
Extended temperature range: The specified -40°C to +105°C operating range supports designs exposed to a broad range of environmental temperatures.

**Compact package:** The 63-ball VFBGA package helps integrate memory into space-constrained electronic designs.
These benefits must be evaluated alongside the full datasheet, system architecture, and application-specific requirements.

**Design Considerations Before Using This NAND Flash Memory**
Selecting a [flash memory](https://support.cookiebot.com/hc/en-us?brand_id=360000562514) component involves more than checking capacity and voltage. Engineers should verify several technical factors before integrating the MT29F1G08ABAFAH4-AAT into a design.

First, confirm that the processor or NAND controller supports the device's command set, addressing scheme, bus timing, and electrical interface.

Second, check whether error correction is required. NAND flash can develop bit errors, so the controller may need suitable error-correction code (ECC) capabilities. Do not assume that all error correction is handled internally; verify the exact device documentation.

Third, consider bad-block management, wear management, data retention, and power-loss behavior. These factors are particularly important in products that store firmware or frequently update persistent information.

Finally, confirm the package footprint, voltage limits, environmental requirements, and the exact ordering suffix. Components with similar part numbers may have different package, temperature, or electrical characteristics.

**Why Choose a Suitable NAND Flash Memory Supplier?**
Finding the correct memory component is an important part of reliable electronic product development. Engineers and procurement teams should evaluate manufacturer documentation, traceability, component condition, and availability before purchasing semiconductor memory.

For engineers researching embedded memory solutions,[ globX](https://globx.eu/) provides an online platform for exploring electronic components and sourcing requirements. Buyers can also visit the[ globX electronics blog](https://globx.eu/blog) for additional information about semiconductor devices, component specifications, and electronic sourcing topics.
Always verify the exact part number and its current datasheet before making a purchase or approving a component for production.

**Conclusion**
The Micron MT29F1G08ABAFAH4-AAT NAND flash memory provides 1Gb of non-volatile SLC storage through an eight-bit parallel interface. Its 3.3V I/O specification, compact VFBGA package, and extended operating temperature range make it relevant to compatible embedded, industrial, and automotive electronic designs.
Understanding NAND programming, reading, erasing, and memory-management requirements helps engineers determine whether this component meets their system's storage needs. For accurate implementation, always consult the manufacturer's datasheet and verify interface compatibility, error-correction requirements, and operating conditions.
Explore electronic components and sourcing information at[ globX](https://globx.eu/) to support your next electronic design or procurement project.

**Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)**
1. What is the Micron MT29F1G08ABAFAH4-AAT?
It is a 1Gb SLC NAND flash memory device with an eight-bit parallel data interface, designed for non-volatile storage in compatible electronic systems.
2. How much data can this NAND flash memory store?
Its nominal capacity is 1 gigabit, equivalent to approximately 128 megabytes of raw binary storage.
3. Does the MT29F1G08ABAFAH4-AAT retain data without power?
Yes. NAND flash is non-volatile memory, so it retains stored information without continuous electrical power, subject to specified data-retention conditions.
4. What is SLC NAND flash memory?
SLC stands for single-level cell. It stores one bit per memory cell and is commonly used where endurance and dependable embedded storage are important.
5. What is the operating temperature range of this device?
The manufacturer's specifications list an operating temperature range of -40°C to +105°C.
6. What interface does this Micron memory use?
It uses a parallel NAND interface with an eight-bit data bus. The host processor or memory controller must be compatible with the device's electrical and timing requirements.
7. Can NAND flash memory be overwritten directly?
Typically, NAND flash must be erased in blocks before the affected storage can be reprogrammed. The host system must manage erase and program operations correctly.
8. Is the MT29F1G08ABAFAH4-AAT suitable for automotive electronics?
Its extended temperature range makes it a candidate for suitable automotive applications. Engineers should still confirm the exact ordering code, qualification requirements, and system-level compatibility before use.

## Same-run money-in discovery/qualification — 2026-10-12 (SAST)

This updates the existing Category A request, not a new queue or worker. The country-origin/legitimacy rule is applied only to income opportunities; it does not constrain continuity-drive mapping/noding/weighting.

### Results that change ranking

**1. Current South Africa micro-work route — TELUS Digital Online Data Analyst**
- Official role page remains live: https://jobs.telusdigital.com/jobs/18301194-online-data-analyst-south-africa
- Primary-source readback says freelance/part-time map-data verification, standard assessment, and five consecutive years' residence in South Africa are required.
- This is an existing ledger provider/role, not a newly discovered independent source. It remains an application/assessment route, not assigned work or earnings. Keep distinct from other providers; preserve the existing OTP/identity/application gate. No new application was sent.

**2. OneForma — existing provider, not multiple independent income routes**
- Official payout rules: https://www.oneforma.com/help-center/payment-issues-and-finance/how-payments-work-on-oneforma/
- Pay cycle is project-dependent weekly/bi-weekly; typically 2–3 business days after cycle when a payout account is connected; typical minimum USD $10 equivalent; Payoneer/PayPal/Tipalti are region-dependent.
- Existing South Africa qualification case CAS-76245-N9W2F5 has no substantive project/rate/eligibility answer in the last recorded mail reconciliation. No task assignment is evidenced. Do not rank its project count as cash-ready opportunity volume.

**3. Prolific — legitimate but not a near-term cash route while waitlisted**
- Official cash-out instructions: https://participant-help.prolific.com/en/articles/445062-how-do-i-cash-out-on-prolific
- A low cash-out threshold is not enough to make it executable; researcher approval can keep rewards pending, and the current account/study access gate remains decisive. Existing ledger status remains deprioritized pending actual access and current study availability.

**4. Web3: 1inch Infrastructure Bug Bounty — real, rules-defined, but low-probability and capability-gated**
- Official Immunefi program: https://immunefi.com/bug-bounty/1inch-infrastructure/information/
- Page was current to 9 Oct 2026; indicates USDC on Ethereum payouts, KYC required, proof-of-concept required, and a USD $20,000 maximum with tiered rewards. This is a bounty for a valid in-scope security vulnerability—not paid hourly work and not a reward for simply participating.
- Public 1inch Business terms name Degensoft Ltd, BVI: https://business.1inch.com/portal/terms-of-service. That helps identify a related legal entity, but the evidence retrieved here does not conclusively bind that entity to this exact bounty's paying counterparty. **Disposition: HOLD for payer/entity binding and only advance if an in-scope issue is actually supported by existing authorized testing capability.** No probing, exploit, account/KYC disclosure or wallet transaction was performed. Do not put this ahead of direct paid pilots.

### Rejected/discounted noise

- Superteam “Explain Market Tokenization in Your Country” page: https://superteam.fun/earn/listing/explain-market-tokenization-in-your-country — despite a displayed 5,500 USDC prize headline and global eligibility, its rules explicitly say winners receive a Breakpoint ticket **in place of the prize amount; no cash**. It also showed 94 submissions and announcement on 13 Oct. **REJECT for money-in.**
- Superteam's older high-headline listings that were checked in this run were either Canada-only, past their winner dates, dependent on attending an already-completed event, or required buying/holding a token. They are not counted as current withdrawable-money routes.
- Current Superteam agent/content contests are competitive winner pools, not paid task contracts. A USDC label or total prize pool does not mean a participant has a receivable. Do not advance them unless sponsor/payer origin, live deadline, rules and payout are verified and expected net value beats direct buyer work.
- A PeoplePerHour AI automation listing advertising about USD $374 was not independently inspectable because the page served an anti-bot interstitial; the accessible card alone did not establish the buyer/payee identity or funding/escrow state. After that bounded verification attempt, **DISCARD rather than leave active HOLD**. No bid was made.
- Recent Reddit “for-hire” search results were supply-side developer adverts, not buyers offering to pay. Excluded as non-opportunities.

### Existing global crypto inventory
Latest confirmed first-party Agent Bounties snapshot in the existing Category A record is dated 11 Oct: 0 claimable, 0 verification-ready and $0 funded USDC; some nominal items were explicitly not verifier-ready. The 12 Oct external refresh was not independently read back in this run, so this remains **stale prior evidence, not a claim about today's inventory**. Do not count nominal mirror/feed entries until current primary inventory, eligibility, payout and settlement route are independently read back.

### Direct paid-pilot lane
- Existing canonical opportunities remain the priority: Kingston Stanley ($99 / 48-hour sourcing overflow pilot) and Xubio ($49 / 48-hour onboarding support pilot) already sent and followed up once; OnTrack Mulching cleanup offer sent; JobNect/KJ Plumbing remain delivery-delayed; Colonia Estudio, Cork City Gaol and Cuina Teva were rejected/closed to unsolicited follow-up; MPRTC route is known wrong/unmonitored. Respect each record's current contact state—do not re-contact merely because revenue is slow.
- The two existing Upwork briefs (USD $700 RAG/CRM build and USD $1,000 WhatsApp/GHL agent) remain gated on a truthful live demo/source proof and authorized authenticated proposal route. Do not call either applied or qualified.
- The public searches in this bounded run produced no additional direct buyer brief that met all requirements (identifiable payer, live scope, feasible route from South Africa and credible short path to withdrawable payment). Supply-side posts and expired posts were excluded. This is not a claim that no such buyer exists; discovery remains open.

### Execution/acceptance report
- **New routes fully qualified as near-term withdrawable money:** 0.
- **New Web3 route held for one bounded verification / capability gate:** 1 (1inch Infrastructure Bounty).
- **Rejected as non-cash, stale/ineligible, unverifiable, or supply-side noise:** multiple, as above.
- **Applications, bids, outreach, purchases, wallet transactions or paid tasks executed in this research pass:** 0.
- **Revenue or Owner repayment evidenced by this pass:** $0. No repayment is claimed.
- **Next actions:** maintain focus on current warm/direct pilot responses and current unblocked paid-task gates; recheck live microtask availability via first-party routes; get current funded/claimable bounty inventory via its authorized API surface; only retain Web3 candidates with scope fit and transparent payer/control/settlement. Continue to reject unverifiable offerings after one bounded public-source check.

The 33% allocation remains a governance request until ROOT/T-GOV disposition and per-worker consumption/behavioral receipts are read back. ASK: HN Help and Forward Advice, Ideas: New Lossless cmpr MRT/CT, Astro
Hey HN, at first, i'm not from that subject field so I dont know what to do. I'm an ordinary engeneer with basics and unorthodox thinking. I used Claude to help me implement. Its a process of several months and bazills of millions of tokens of work. I can't show or disclose, begging for your understanding. I can't beat WEBP lossless on kodak test suite, YET; But I'm like 5% worser on RGBa. CMYK's similar. Here, the advantage is me being 5-15x faster as WEBP / other lossless codecs. Not yet fully confirmed, but promissing results WEBP will be knocked too. My lossy compression is better than JPEG sometimes, but always ~10++ times faster. Very big building field right now. The figures are very promissing on lossless video. On cpu cycles beating every SOTA methods by being upto 15x faster or so. Possible path. My lossy shows better sharpness and details in (very) fast moving scenes (1080p, 2k, 4k incl. hdr), while being only ~5-10% bigger than heif and avc, and others with comperable compression params. May be is resolved in x-xx weeks. → noticed, my lossless works better as SOTA (JPEG LS, JPEG 2000 and JPEG XL, each lossless mode) on medical imaging / DICOM, voluminetric medical/scientific data, handles pixel bitdepths >32bit; >32000x32000px (jpeg didnt even consume). It seems to scale res/depth without issues. Runs on data from various MRT/CT Imagers and formats found for download show ~15%-50% percent better compression as SOTA/DICOM, at a fraction of cycles. Some results: CT volumes, ratio and (encode / decode seconds) - pancreas, 185 slices →  3.26 (0.7 / 0.6)  │ JPEG-LS: 2.69 (2.3 / 1.8) │ JPEG 2000: 2.71 (10.6 / 8.5) │ FFV1: 2.70 - COVID chest, 2464 slices →  4.48 (10.0 / 8.6)  │ JPEG-LS: 3.30 (24.6 / 18.9) │ JPEG 2000: 3.12 (129 / 101) │ FFV1: 3.21 - Colonography, 950 slices →  2.79, was 2.59  │ JPEG-LS: 2.73 (10.9 / 8.8) │ JPEG 2000: 2.61 (55.6 / 44.2) │ FFV1: 2.99 - LIDC lung, 764 slices, 12-bit →  2.67 (3.1 / 2.8)  │ JPEG-LS: 2.40 (9.9 / 7.7) │ JPEG 2000: 2.40 (46.1 / 37.9) │ FFV1: 2.37 - TCGA kidney, 820 slices →  3.31 (3.3 / 2.9)  │ JPEG-LS: 2.87 (9.2 / 7.1) │ JPEG 2000: 2.74 (48.1 / 37.3) │ FFV1: 2.80 MR and SAR data is also a possible play field with some prommissing results I've already seen. So, as everyone too, i want $$$. I decided to walk my own way after being fired in 2 mins two years ago and I dont have much financial reserves left, without getting income atm. Can't start employment; Need & Want to fight with Claude 23h/7d instead on other ideas I'm working on since years. Need MONEY!! So, if you would be me. Open Sourcing the algorithm is bread-less and doesn't pay my/your bills. I'm seeking Advice or Ideas on how would you approach it, if you were me - with max profit in the head (.. but still do good!). The actual and future storage/memory crisis opens up a lever. My approach puts together: storage AND compute can both be siginificantly reduced. - AWS health services, google health and some other smaller cloud service providers - Medical imaging device producers (mrt/ct) saving on cpu and memory - Physicians using SaaS for storage/viewing - Astro/Scientific imaging and processing - Possible space/SAR/satelite imaging/data, not giving up on it yet. But how to approach?? If you give it to x, then y will need it too for processing x's data. This gives a conflict in interest. Interest is profit max. What could end up as a strategy? How to find someone to pitch? Selling? Licensing? Other models? Patenting may not work / doesn't use patented methods. Appreciate any answer and 'thank you' to everyone reading. If I dont respond to your comment, think of me saying 'thank you' while bowing very deeply, weaving my hat. This post is not meant to let others do my work, its a scream for direction - kind of desperate & blind

source_text:
If-node in sub-workflow causes properties of previous node to become not found when all items go the false path
### Bug Description

The properties of an earlier node can become not found. This Problem occurs when between the node that sets the property and the node that tries to access it there is a sub-workflow and inside that sub-workflow there is an if-node and all items inside the sub-workflow will go the false path of the if-node.

The error does not occur if all items of the sub-workflow will go the true path or if some items go true and others go false.

Also the property seems to be not found if the expression uses "item" to reference a previous node. When using "first()" or "all()[0]" it seems to work.

Maybe related: When debugging an execution where all items in an if-node use the false path and a merge node is behind it, the merge node is unable to execute.

### To Reproduce

[main-workflow.json](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33341808/main-workflow.json)
[sub-workflow.json](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33341809/sub-workflow.json)

These json files show a main-workflow and a sub-workflow to reproduce this issue. 
If the value properties of all items in the "Set Array Data" nodes myItems field  is true, the workflow works. But if all are set to false the code node at the end will throw an error and in the edit fiels node at the end you can see the difference between the expressions.

### Expected behavior

After the described sub-workflow, nodes should still be able to access earlier nodes via the " $('NameOfEarlyNode').item.json " expression, even if all items used the false path in the subworkflow.
